reason: The locked test e2e/settings.spec.ts 'every Settings control is reachable by Tab, native, keyboard-operable and at least 44x44' (owner TASK-12.1) cannot pass with D-4 edits 1-3 only. Its tabOrder walk starts from the focused Settings h1, which comes after '← Home' in the DOM (header: ← Home, then h1). So Tab reaches the checkbox first (the next control after the h1), then leaves the page, then wraps to '← Home'. The walk returns ['Show opponent styles at the table', '← Home'], but `expected` (DOM order from controls.evaluateAll, edit 3) is ['← Home', 'Show opponent styles at the table']. With only ← Home (TASK-12.1) the rotation was invisible because there was one control. SPEC-09's sentence 'Tab reaches ← Home then the checkbox' does not hold from the focused heading.
evidence: Full Playwright run (npm run build && npx playwright test): 338 passed, 18 skipped, 2 failed. Both failures are this test at e2e/settings.spec.ts:80 `expect(order).toEqual(expected)` with Received ['Show opponent styles at the table', '← Home'] vs Expected ['← Home', 'Show opponent styles at the table'] in chromium and webkit. A temporary probe (deleted) from the focused h1 gave the focus sequence INPUT, BODY, BUTTON, INPUT in both browsers. The checkbox input's bounding box is 44x44 in both, so the unchanged size, tag and Enter/Space assertions would pass. Every other e2e passes, including all 4 tests in e2e/opponent-styles.spec.ts in both browsers.
options: (Recommended) Allow a 4th locked edit that keeps the assertion exact: compare the walk with the sequence from the focused heading, e.g. `expect(order).toEqual([...expected.slice(1), expected[0]])` (the controls after the h1 in DOM order, then the wrap to ← Home), or literally ['Show opponent styles at the table', '← Home']. Nothing is loosened: every control must still be reached exactly once, in a fixed order.

Allow a 4th locked edit that starts the walk before ← Home (e.g. focus a point before the header first) so the walk follows DOM order. This is less robust: Chromium and WebKit treat the sequential focus starting point differently after a blur.
Change the product so the h1 comes before ← Home in the DOM (ordered visually with CSS). Not recommended: DOM/focus order would no longer match visual order (WCAG 2.4.3), and it is outside the spec.
